thread:
Alex K: Kicking off config-only deploy now — routing policy change + idle-timeout reduction. Rolling canary at 10% for 20m. No model or binary changes.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: config/deploys/1699004321. Canary shard set: t=10%. Watch for 5xx and latency spikes. :rocket:

Samir: quick q — are we pinning to the previous routing snapshot for fallback?

Alex K: Yes. Canary will route to new policy but we keep a pinned snapshot (snapshot:v2023.11-routing) for immediate rollback.

Mira Patel: Observability checklist copied here: - perf dash: /dash/route-latency - error budget alerts enabled - canary trace sampling up to 100% for 10m.

Samir: ack. Also lowering idle-timeout from 6s -> 2s, and tightening per-route token limit 5000->3000. Is that safe for long-lived streams? :thinking:

Alex K: Streams should be fine; this only affects free idle periods. Batching window unchanged (50ms). See config snippet:

```
routing:
  policy: prefer-fast-path
  snapshot: v2023.11-routing
limits:
  per_route_tokens: 3000
  idle_timeout_ms: 2000
batching:
  max_batch_ms: 50
  concurrency: auto
```

deploy-bot: Canary healthy at 10% (0 errors, p95 latency +1ms). Monitoring for 20m.

oncall-bot: If error rate > 0.5% for 5m, automatic rollback triggered.

Mira Patel: If we need a manual rollback, steps: 1) pin traffic to snapshot:v2023.11-routing (console) 2) revert config in repo and tag rollback-1699004321 3) run quick smoke on preflight route. I'll be oncall for next 30m.

Samir: Sounds good. I'll keep an eye on ephemeral queue depth. :eyes:

Alex K: Thanks all — calling this thread closed unless alerts pop. :thumbsup:
